result:
The web interface's XSRF cookie is now named `_mitmproxy_xsrf`, both where the server sets it and where the frontend reads it. I didn't run any tests or the frontend build.

- **Server:** in `mitmproxy/tools/web/app.py` I added `xsrf_cookie_name="_mitmproxy_xsrf"` to the Tornado `Application` settings. Tornado uses this name when it sets the cookie and when it validates the `X-XSRFToken` header and the form field.
- **Frontend:** in `web/src/js/utils.ts` the `xsrf()` helper now calls `getCookie("_mitmproxy_xsrf")`, so it reads the new cookie.
- **Changelog:** I added an entry to `CHANGELOG.md`.

The new name means browsers stop sending the old `_xsrf` cookie that broke Firefox, and they get a fresh cookie under the new name.

The compiled bundle in `mitmproxy/tools/web/static/` still reads `_xsrf`. It is a build artifact, so it needs a frontend rebuild before the frontend and server agree. I didn't add a test, since the existing tests turn XSRF checking off.
